title: Monolithic Conditional Dispatch Loop (Conditional Dispatcher)
pattern: A dispatcher executes actions directly within a monolithic conditional structure (match/switch statement) branching on a string, enum, or command identifier.
why_bad: Violates the Open-Closed Principle. Adding, removing, or changing an action requires modifying the central dispatcher class, raising cognitive load and introducing risks of regression in unrelated action pathways.
detection: A control handler contains a single large match or switch statement routing requests to localized business logic blocks.
counterexample: Simple, localized routing in minor internal components or simple parser command mapping where action implementations are delegating to external classes directly without holding business state. Marked `Context-dependent`.
source: Joshua Kerievsky, *Refactoring to Patterns* (2004), Chapter 6, "Replace Conditional Dispatcher with Command", p. 376-377.
